screen: LMS → Learning Dashboard + Learning Catalog (unit: lms-dash-catalog)
screenLevelGaps: CONFIRMED, AND WORSE THAN SUSPECTED — there is NO skills-to-course mapping field on the course form. course-form-sheet.tsx FormState (L27-38) is exactly ten fields: display_name, standard_id, subject_category, subject_type, subject_code, short_name, jobrole, sort_order, certificate_validity_months, status. No skill picker, no competency picker, no KASBA picker, no proficiency, no learning objectives. The ONLY course->skill link that exists in the whole schema is the single-valued column sub_std_map.subject_id, which SkillDevelopmentController.php:108-111 joins to s_users_skills.id and LmsLearningController.php:965-984 (resolveCourseSkillId) reads to stamp lms_certificates.skill_id. Neither POST /api/lms/courses (LmsCourseController.php:682-703) nor PUT /api/lms/courses/{id} (L822-836) nor POST /api/lms/ai/outlines/{id}/publish (AiCourseController.php:564-579) ever writes subject_id. Therefore EVERY course created through any UI in this unit has subject_id = NULL, is invisible to Skill Progress, and produces certificates with skill_id NULL. The spec's auto-recommendation engine genuinely has nothing to point to.

The skill link is also structurally wrong even where it exists: subject_id is ONE nullable bigint, so a course can build at most one skill. Real courses build several. There is no course_skills join table anywhere (verified: no migration in database/migrations matches a course<->skill many-to-many).

CONFIRMED — courses live in the K-12 sub_std_map table. database/migrations/2025_06_02_093430_create_sub_std_map_table.php declares FOREIGN KEY subject_id -> subject.id and FOREIGN KEY standard_id -> standard.id (the K-12 grade table). Every LMS query instead joins standard_id to hrms_departments (LmsCourseController.php:295, :499, :561) and treats subject_id as an s_users_skills id. So both foreign keys point at tables the application no longer means. The columns subject_code/subject_type/short_name/jobrole/proficiency the catalog reads and writes have no migration at all in this tree except proficiency (2026_03_10_102100) — the rest exist only in the legacy imported schema.

DATA LOSS ON EVERY COURSE EDIT: LmsCourseController@update (L822-836) writes 'proficiency' => $request->proficiency unconditionally, but course-form-sheet.tsx handleSubmit (L189-203) builds a payload with no proficiency key. Editing any course from the catalog silently NULLs sub_std_map.proficiency — the only field that says what level of capability the course targets, and the field /available_courses (LmsCourseEnrollController.php:175) returns to the enrol picker.

'Learning Hours' KPI (lms-dashboard.tsx:222) and 'Current Streak' (insight-widgets.tsx:425) are not learning metrics at all. SkillDevelopmentController@getWeeklyLearningGoal (L405-422) sums hrms_attendances punchin/punchout hours and caps them at a hardcoded 12; @getLearningStreak (L267-276) counts consecutive hrms_attendances punch-in days. A learner who never opens a course but clocks in daily shows a 30-day 'learning streak' and 12h of 'learning hours'. Goal values 12 and 30 are hardcoded, not configurable.

'Skill Progress' widget is a competency-rating readout mislabelled as learning progress. SkillDevelopmentController.php:148 computes progress_percentage = AVG(s_skill_matrix.skill_level)/5*100. Completing a course NEVER moves that bar — no LMS endpoint writes s_skill_matrix (re-verified across LmsCourseEnrollController, LmsCourseController, LmsLearningController, AiCourseController). The 'x of y courses completed' caption underneath comes from a different query, so the bar and the caption can disagree indefinitely.

TWO DIVERGENT COMPLETION PATHS. The dashboard kebab 'Mark as completed' (course-widgets.tsx:220) PUTs /api/enroll/{id}, which sets lms_course_enroll.status only (LmsCourseEnrollController.php:449-458) — no completed_at, no lms_content_progress, no certificate. The real completion path is lms_content_progress (LmsLearningController.php:346-352) and issueCertificate (L1424-1443) which refuses unless every content_master row for the course is complete. So a learner can self-declare a course complete from the dashboard, have it counted in the 'Completed Courses' KPI, the transcript, the achievements query and the catalog's completion_rate, while being provably unable to claim the certificate.

AUTHORIZATION BYPASS: approval-required enrolments are self-approvable from this screen. Enrolling on a course whose lms_course_settings.enrollment_rule='approval' stores status='pending' (LmsCourseEnrollController.php:365). use-lms-dashboard.ts toDashboardCourse (L72-82) does not recognise 'pending' and files it under 'not-started', where the kebab menu offers 'Move to in progress' and 'Mark as completed'. @update (L419-425) validates only status in:completed,in-progress and looks the row up by id+user_id — it never checks the current status — so the learner flips their own pending request to approved.

CROSS-TENANT READ on the dashboard's primary data source: LmsCourseEnrollController@index resolves $subInstituteId at L36 and then NEVER USES IT. $userId comes from $request->user_id (L38), so GET /api/enrolled_courses?user_id=<anyone> returns that person's full course list, enrolment ids, dates and department regardless of organisation. @available (L117) has the same request-trusted user_id.

Achievements are computed from the wrong column and the earned date is fabricated. SkillDevelopmentController.php:493 filters courses_completed_month with DATE_FORMAT(end_date,'%Y-%m') — end_date is the enrolment WINDOW end (the due date the frontend hardcodes as today+60 days, use-lms-dashboard.ts:35), not a completion date. L531 then sets earned_date = now()->format('d/m/Y'), so every earned badge always reads 'Earned <today>'.

Two of the three calendar API calls the dashboard fires are wasted. use-lms-dashboard.ts:276-277 fetches this month and next month, sorts them into `upcomingEvents` (L310-322) and exposes it (L537) — but lms-dashboard.tsx destructures at L96-120 without upcomingEvents and nothing renders it. LmsCalendarWidget is fed by a separate third fetch (loadCalendar, L365). Dead state, three round-trips for one visible calendar.

The AI sheet's 'Target skills', 'Key tasks', 'Critical work function' and 'Proficiency' inputs are prompt-only. AiCourseController.php:189-200 folds skills into the DeepSeek prompt as target_skills and discards them; @publish (L503-513) validates only display_name/standard_id/subject_category/subject_type/jobrole/status and inserts none of them. The one screen in the product that asks an author which skills a course builds throws that answer away.

An AI-published course is uncompletable and uncertifiable. AiCourseController@publish (L564-579) inserts a sub_std_map row and nothing else — no chapter_master, no content_master. LmsLearningController@issueCertificate (L1424-1443) rejects any course with total content = 0 ('Courses with no content cannot be certified'). The Gamma deck stays on ai_course_outlines.gamma_url and is never attached to the course learners enrol in.

The catalog course form exposes NONE of the lms_course_settings fields the API accepts. LmsCourseController@settingsRules (L117-141) supports description, duration_minutes, language, is_mandatory, discussion_enabled, visibility, passing_score, max_attempts, issue_certificate, certificate_template, recert_alerts, enrollment_rule, restrict_departments, restrict_roles, available_from/until and prerequisites; the form sends none of them. Courses authored here are therefore always open-enrolment, unrestricted, undated, with no duration and no description. GET /api/lms/courses/{id} returns settings+prerequisites (L595) and course-details-sheet.tsx ignores the whole block.

The Enroll sheet lists courses the server will refuse. @available (L142-161) filters only on tenant, deleted_at and status=1; visibility, restrict_departments, restrict_roles, available_from/until and prerequisites are enforced only at enrol time by checkEnrolmentEligibility (L207-317). Every restricted course is shown with a live Enroll button that 422s.

The 'Recent Activity' feed can display the wrong course name. SkillDevelopmentController.php:840 does leftJoin('subject as subj','s.subject_id','=','subj.id') then COALESCE(subj.subject_name, s.display_name) — but subject_id is a skill/task/jobrole id in this schema (the controller says so itself at L106-111). Any collision with a `subject` row id substitutes a K-12 subject name for the course title.

'Chapters' in the details sheet counts chapter_master WHERE subject_id = sub_std_map.id (LmsCourseController.php:588-590), while chapter_master.subject_id carries a declared FK to subject.id (2025_06_02_093441 migration) and the legacy chapterController.php:553 joins it that way. The two id spaces are used interchangeably in the same codebase; this tile is correct only by accident of which writer produced the rows.

Nothing on either screen connects a course to Talent Management, Performance, Task Management or the competency framework. The only competency link that exists in the LMS schema is lms_assignments.competency_id, added by 2026_07_29_100300 for the Competency module's Development Plan tab (source='competency') — i.e. competency reaches INTO LMS to assign a course, but a course still cannot declare what it builds, and LMS never reports back.

The recommendation store that does exist is task-keyed and write-only. suggested_course lost its skill_id column (migration 2026_02_02_061152) and SuggestedCourseController exposes a single store() method requiring task_id — there is no read endpoint, no gap-to-course query, and no UI in this unit that writes or reads it.

No compliance or certification surface on either screen: certificate_validity_months is authorable in the form (course-form-sheet.tsx:328) but is never displayed in the catalog table, the details sheet, the transcript or any dashboard widget, and no widget shows an expiring certificate — despite lms_certificates carrying expires_at and a derived expiry_state (LmsLearningController.php:1011-1012).

peer-comparison is an N+1 over the entire tenant: SkillDevelopmentController.php:609-624 plucks every tbluser id and runs calculateUserProgress (a 2-table aggregate) once per user, per dashboard load, to fill one caption.

Catalog authoring is gated client-side on user.role === 'admin' || 'hr' (learning-catalog.tsx:151) but LmsCourseController's store/update/destroy/bulk have NO role guard — only guardApiToken. Any token holder can POST/PUT/DELETE /api/lms/courses. (Contrast AiCourseController@publish:497 which does call guardAuthoring.)

features.purpose: Target job role for the course
features.shouldFeed: Organization job-role master; Competency role profile
features.gap: Not a foreign key — see the Job role filter entry
The aggregate subquery is not tenant-filtered (LmsCourseController.php:78-86); it is safe only because course_id already scopes it

features.purpose: Share of that course's learners who completed
features.shouldFeed: Course-effectiveness analytics; Competency (does this course actually close gaps?)
features.gap: Measures throughput only. Because a completion here can be self-declared with no content consumed and no assessment, a 100% completion rate is not evidence the course works. No pre/post competency delta is computed anywhere.
No owner column and no 'review due' concept — the table cannot answer 'which courses are stale and who owns them'

features.element: Table missing column: Skills / competencies built
features.purpose: Would show what capability each course develops
features.shouldFeed: Competency gap -> course recommendation; Talent Mgmt role readiness
features.gap: Does not exist. There is no column, no filter and no sort for skills anywhere in the catalog, because sub_std_map has no skills field the UI can populate. An HR admin cannot answer 'which courses build Skill X'.
Uses a rotated ListFilter icon rather than a standard kebab/ellipsis — reads as a filter control

features.reads: full sub_std_map row + chapter_count + settings + prerequisites
features.gap: The response also carries `settings` and `prerequisites` (LmsCourseController.php:595) and the drawer discards both

features.purpose: Open the form in edit mode
features.gap: Prefills from the LIST row, not the detail fetch, so any field the list select omits is invisible to the editor — and the save then writes null over it (see the proficiency data-loss finding)
No confirmation for a single-row deactivate even though enrolled learners are affected

features.purpose: Open details for the clicked course
Select rows for bulk actions (admin/HR only)
features.gap: Selection persists across page/filter changes — see the bulk counter entry

features.purpose: Page through the catalogue, 10 per page
features.reads: meta.total from a cloned COUNT query
features.gap: per_page is hardcoded to 10 by useCourseCatalog(10) with no page-size control, even though the API accepts up to 100

features.element: Table empty state (+ Clear filters / New Course)
features.purpose: Distinguishes 'no matches' from 'no courses yet' and offers the right action

features.shouldFeed: Competency development plans and lms_assignments referencing the course
features.gap: Copy says 'Existing enrolments are kept' — accurate but the consequence is orphaned enrolments pointing at a soft-deleted course, and lms_assignments.course_id / lms_course_prerequisites.prerequisite_course_id are not cleaned up or blocked. Deleting a course that is another course's prerequisite leaves that course permanently un-enrollable.

features.shouldFeed: Same downstream cleanups as single delete
features.gap: Same orphaning, at scale. The 'skipped' count the API returns (ids belonging to another tenant) is discarded by the client.
Real FK to hrms_departments in application terms, but the DB-declared FK on standard_id points at the K-12 `standard` table
No retry — the user must close and reopen the drawer
Not clickable — an admin cannot see WHO is enrolled from here

features.purpose: Number of chapters in the course
features.gap: chapter_master.subject_id has a declared FK to subject.id (2025_06_02_093441 migration) and legacy chapterController.php:553 joins it that way, while this count treats it as a sub_std_map id. The two id spaces are used interchangeably in the same codebase; a 0 here may mean 'no chapters' or 'wrong id space'.

features.element: Details: Completion % + bar + 'x of y completed'
features.gap: Same caveat as the table column — counts self-declared completions
Free string, not a reference
Duplicates the heading subtitle at L133

sort_order is not one of the SORTABLE columns (LmsCourseController.php:38-46) and no list in this unit orders by it — the catalog, the enrol sheet and My Learning all ignore it. It is authorable and displayed but has no effect anywhere.
created_by / updated_by are stored by the API but never shown — the drawer cannot say who authored the course

features.element: Details missing: certificate validity, settings block, prerequisites, skills
features.purpose: Would show what the course requires, issues and builds
features.gap: certificate_validity_months is authorable in the form and never displayed anywhere; the settings and prerequisites arrays are fetched and dropped on the floor; there is no skills row because no skills data exists

features.purpose: Open the form in edit mode (admin/HR only)
features.gap: Passes the LIST `course`, not the fetched `detail`, so the form is prefilled from the thinner object

features.purpose: Trigger the delete confirmation from the drawer

features.gap: Client validation mirrors the server rules (required, max 191); uniqueness of name+department is server-only and surfaces as a 422 banner

features.api: options from GET /api/lms/courses/filters; written by POST/PUT
features.reads: hrms_departments rows that already own a course in this tenant
features.shouldFeed: Organization department master (the real source of truth)
features.gap: The options list is derived from departments that ALREADY have a course (LmsCourseController.php:498-505 inner-joins sub_std_map), so a department with no courses yet can never be chosen — a brand-new customer cannot create their first course for most of their org. The API also returns course_count to disambiguate same-named departments and this select drops it, rendering identical labels.

Free text by design (no master table). Critically, this same column is the discriminator the skill join uses ('task'/'jobrole'/'course'/'sub' are reserved sentinels, SkillDevelopmentController.php:110) — an author typing 'Task' here silently excludes the course from skill progress, and nothing in the UI warns them.
Free text, so modality is unnormalised and cannot drive any behaviour (e.g. instructor-led courses do not require a session)
Not unique-constrained — two courses can share a code
Written but never displayed in the catalog table, the enrol sheet, My Learning or the transcript — only in the details drawer

features.element: Form field: Job role (free text + datalist)
features.purpose: sub_std_map.jobrole — the closest thing to a competency link
features.shouldFeed: Organization s_user_jobrole master; Competency role->skill profile; Talent Mgmt role readiness
features.gap: Marked 'Optional' and stored as a free string. Suggestions come from strings already typed into sub_std_map, NOT from the organisation's job-role master — so the datalist propagates typos rather than constraining to real roles. This is the field a role-based recommendation engine would have to key on, and it cannot be trusted.
Nothing in this unit (or the enrol picker, or My Learning) sorts by sort_order — the value is captured and never used

features.shouldFeed: lms_certificates.expires_at -> compliance/recertification alerts -> HRIT and Competency certification requirements
features.gap: The value IS consumed by issueCertificate to set expires_at, so the write is real — but it is displayed nowhere in this unit, the dashboard has no expiring-certificate widget, and the recert_alerts setting that would act on it is not exposed by this form

features.element: Form field: Cover image (create-only file input)
features.purpose: Upload the course thumbnail to DigitalOcean
features.gap: Deliberately hidden in edit mode because PUT does not accept uploads — a course's image can therefore never be changed or removed after creation. No size or dimension validation beyond Laravel's `image` rule.
Helper text is accurate ('Inactive courses stay in the catalog but are not offered to learners' — matches @available's status=1 filter)

features.element: Form MISSING field: Skills / competencies this course builds
features.api: NONE — POST/PUT do not accept a skills key
features.shouldFeed: Competency gap analysis -> auto course recommendation; certificate.skill_id; Skill Progress widget; Talent Mgmt readiness
features.gap: THE headline finding, confirmed field by field. The only usable link, sub_std_map.subject_id, is absent from FormState, absent from CourseCreatePayload/CourseUpdatePayload (services/lms/catalog.ts:131-148) and absent from the controller's insert/update arrays. Every course created here is permanently unmapped to any skill.

features.element: Form MISSING field: Proficiency level targeted
features.purpose: sub_std_map.proficiency — the level of capability the course delivers
features.api: PUT /api/lms/courses/{id} accepts it and the form never sends it
features.writes: NULL — actively destroys the stored value
features.shouldFeed: Competency proficiency scale; gap-to-course matching at the right level
features.gap: Not merely missing: because LmsCourseController@update:830 writes 'proficiency' => $request->proficiency unconditionally, saving any course from this form NULLs the column. The column was added on purpose (migration 2026_03_10_102100) and is returned by /available_courses and the catalog list — this form quietly erases it.

features.element: Form MISSING fields: description, duration, language, mandatory, passing score, max attempts, certificate template, enrolment rule, visibility, restrictions, availability window, prerequisites
features.purpose: The lms_course_settings block the API fully supports
features.writes: nothing (the API's no-key guard means existing settings are preserved, not wiped)
features.shouldFeed: Enrolment gating, compliance, certificate issuance, prerequisite chains
features.gap: Fourteen supported, enforced settings are unreachable from this form. A course authored here can never be mandatory, never require approval, never be restricted to a department, never have a prerequisite and never carry a duration — even though LmsCourseEnrollController@checkEnrolmentEligibility enforces every one of them at enrol time.
No unsaved-changes warning

features.element: Form: Create course / Save changes button
features.gap: Client validation mirrors only 4 of the server's rules; certificate_validity_months has min/max on the input but no client check, so 601 is rejected only by the server

features.gap: Leaks the env var name to any user who opens the sheet

features.purpose: Warns that outlines cannot be rendered to slides
Surfaces generation errors and the rendering-in-progress message
Seed title, or blank to let the model choose

features.shouldFeed: Should be the same department the course is published to
features.gap: This is a free-text prompt field; the actual standard_id comes from a SEPARATE required select at the publish step (L470). The two can disagree with no warning.

features.api: POST /api/lms/ai/outline; also sent as jobrole at publish
features.gap: Persisted, but as the same unconstrained free string as the manual form; also doubles as course_type when building the presentation (L508)

features.purpose: Target proficiency for the generated course
features.gap: The publish payload (L246-254) omits proficiency entirely, even though the column exists and the manual form's absence of it is already a known defect. The value influences the prompt and is then discarded.

features.purpose: CWF context — a core competency-framework concept
features.shouldFeed: Competency framework (CWF is a framework entity, not free prose)
features.gap: Typed by hand rather than selected from the competency framework, and discarded after the prompt

features.element: AI field: Key tasks (one per line)
features.purpose: Tasks the course should prepare the learner for
features.shouldFeed: Task Management task master; suggested_course.task_id (which is literally keyed on tasks)
features.gap: suggested_course is task-keyed (migration 2026_02_02_061152 dropped skill_id in favour of task_id), so tasks are the one entity the recommendation table can already join on — and this screen collects them as untyped prose and throws them away

features.purpose: The skills the generated course should build
features.api: POST /api/lms/ai/outline — AiCourseController.php:189 folds them into the prompt as target_skills and drops them
features.shouldFeed: sub_std_map.subject_id / a course_skills table; Competency; the recommendation engine
features.gap: The single most valuable field on either screen and it is write-only-to-a-prompt. It is a comma-separated free-text box, not a picker over the 3,976-row s_users_skills library, so even if it were persisted the strings would not resolve to skill ids. This is the clearest evidence that skills-to-course mapping was designed for and then not built.
min/max are input attributes only; Number(form.slide_count) || 10 silently coerces junk to 10

features.shouldFeed: sub_std_map.subject_type (the delivery modality column that already exists)
features.gap: Publish hardcodes subject_type to 'E-learning Module' (L251) regardless of what the author ticked — selecting Instructor-led still publishes an e-learning module

features.shouldFeed: lms_virtual_classroom (an instructor-led course needs a session)
features.gap: Ticking it creates no session, no trainer assignment and no schedule; the flag is lost

features.gap: The only route from generated deck to actual course material is a human downloading a PDF and re-uploading it through a different screen

features.purpose: Create the sub_std_map row from the outline
features.gap: Writes display_name, standard_id, subject_category, subject_type, jobrole, sort_order, status and nothing else (AiCourseController.php:564-579). No subject_id (skills), no proficiency, no description, no duration, no content and no chapters. The published course is therefore uncompletable and uncertifiable — LmsLearningController@issueCertificate:1424-1443 refuses any course with zero content items.

features.purpose: Reset the wizard to the input step
